A project update that should take 15 minutes somehow takes an hour. Sound familiar?

A lot of that time goes into figuring out what matters before you even start writing. Briefly helps you organize those scattered notes into a clear, useful brief.

https://briefly.garrettsdevdesk.com

Your next project update is probably hiding in five different places: meeting notes, spreadsheets, messages, deadlines, and your own memory.

Getting everything together is often the hardest part. Briefly gives you a place to turn those scattered details into something useful.

https://briefly.garrettsdevdesk.com

One small change can make writing work updates easier: stop trying to organize and polish everything at once.

Collect your rough notes first. Figure out the message second. Then worry about the wording.

That's the kind of workflow I built Briefly to support.

https://briefly.garrettsdevdesk.com

Before sending your next project update, ask four questions:

What changed? What matters now? What's blocked? What happens next?

Answer those clearly and you've already done much of the important work. Briefly helps put those answers into a structured update.

https://briefly.garrettsdevdesk.com

Not every detail from your meeting notes deserves a place in the final update.

Keep the information that explains a decision, highlights a risk, provides useful context, or helps someone take action. The rest can stay in your working notes.

Build a more focused brief with Briefly: https://briefly.garrettsdevdesk.com

A messy first draft is perfectly fine. Sometimes the best starting point is a pile of notes that barely resembles a finished document.

Get everything down, sort through what matters, and shape it into something your reader can use.

That's why I built Briefly.
